meta.theme: platform work read against the classical definition of the firm, which turns on the substitution of instruction for price, so that a platform is a firm that directs without employing, which means the boundary of the firm and the boundary of the employment relation, having coincided for a century, have come apart, and the remedy is a test graded by how much direction was exercised, whose cost is that the measure it needs exists only in the record the platform keeps

meta.reviewer_notes: The passage is built so that the popular description of platform work is stated in the vocabulary of both its friends and its critics, which makes that description available as a wrong answer to the main idea question. The load-bearing sentence is the one naming the two boundaries, and the closing prescription is deliberately followed by the cost it does not remove, so that an option promising consistency or a settled answer overreaches.
meta.tone: analytic, unhurried, practical at the close

quality.adversarial_review: Q1's live rival is the option about two rival accounts being adjudicated, since the opening does put a description against the platforms' conduct; but only one account is ever set out, the other party to the supposed dispute is the author's own definition, and nothing is discarded as the weaker of two. Q2's rival is the option about conflicting decisions in the courts and the consistency a graded test would bring, which borrows the fourth paragraph's remedy and supplies a motive the passage never states; the passage's complaint about classification is that it asks a question of degree in the form of a label, not that different judges answer it differently. Q3's rival is the option about the scale at which bargaining becomes too costly, which is the passage's explanation of why anybody submits to direction and not its definition of a firm, the definition being given two sentences earlier as the substitution of instruction for price. Q4's rival is the option saying a classifying court must reach a different answer from one that graded direction, which overstates: the passage says the two lines have come apart, not that they now point opposite ways in every case.

paragraphs.text: When platforms began matching drivers to passengers by the trip, the arrangement was welcomed and condemned in the same vocabulary. Here, it was said, was the market recovering ground it had lost to the firm: work bought by the job, as it had been bought before the payroll existed, and the organisation dissolving into a run of separate contracts. The description has one awkwardness. Platforms do not behave like markets. A market lets a seller post his price; the platform sets it. A market lets a buyer choose among sellers; the platform allocates. A market treats a refused bargain as information about what a seller is worth; the platform treats it as a fault and records it against him.

The awkwardness disappears once the firm is defined properly. The classical account does not define it by its payroll, its premises or its longevity. It defines it by the substitution of instruction for price: inside a firm, what gets done is settled by one person telling another to do it, and the reason anybody submits to that method is that bargaining over each transaction separately would cost more than the instruction does. By that test a platform is a firm, and an unusually thorough one. It fixes the price, the route, the order in which jobs arrive, the standard the work must reach and the conditions on which a worker is dropped. The one thing it does not do is employ anybody.

That is the change, and it is not the change usually reported. For most of the last century two boundaries lay on top of each other so exactly that nobody had occasion to tell them apart. The first was the boundary of the firm: the line inside which direction takes the place of bargaining. The second was the boundary of the employment relation: the line inside which a set of obligations attaches, covering notice, a floor under pay, liability for injury, the cost of an idle hour. They coincided because direction was administered through a contract of service, and the law, reasonably enough, took the contract as its evidence that direction was being exercised. A platform pulls them apart. The direction is exercised through an interface, the contract states that the worker is in business on his own account, and the obligations, being fixed to the contract rather than to the direction, go where the contract goes.

If that diagnosis is right, the remedy is not the one the courts are being asked for. What is litigated is a question of classification, employee or contractor, one label or the other, with everything turning on which of two boxes a judge decides a man belongs in. Yet the condition those obligations were built to answer, that one party settles the terms while the other absorbs the consequences, is plainly a matter of degree, and it should be answered in degrees. A test that measured how much direction was exercised, and attached obligations in proportion, would fit the facts better than any binary can. The difficulty is that such a test needs a measure, and the only continuous record of how much direction a platform exercises is the record the platform itself keeps. Grading the test does not dispose of the problem of proof. It moves it, from what a worker can be called to what a company can be made to disclose.

questions.target_mistake: reading the opening contrast between description and conduct as a contest between two stated theories, when only one account is ever attributed to anybody else
questions.prediction_target: The learner should be able to say before looking: a received description is tested against conduct, a definition explains the mismatch, and the remedy that follows is given a cost.
questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the way the passage is organised?

options.A: A familiar description is measured against the behaviour it describes, the mismatch is then accounted for, and a remedy is drawn and then priced.
options.B: A popular description is shown to rest on a mistake of fact, and the corrected facts are then used to defend the test the courts already apply.
options.C: Two rival accounts of an institution are set out at length, the weaker is discarded, and the stronger is extended to a case its authors never foresaw.
options.D: An economic change is described, the losses it has caused are counted, and the reader is warned that the law will be slow to catch up with it.

explanation.expert_notice: Each paragraph announces its own job. The first sets a description beside the conduct and calls the gap an awkwardness; the second says the awkwardness disappears once the firm is defined properly; the third names what has actually changed; the fourth draws a remedy and then states the difficulty the remedy leaves standing.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option tracks those four moves in order and leaves nothing over. The testing is done by the three market comparisons about price, allocation and refusal; the accounting for the mismatch is the recovery of the classical definition; the remedy is the test graded by degree of direction; and the pricing is the closing observation that the measure such a test needs sits in the platform's own records. A structural description earns its place only if every paragraph has a slot in it.
explanation.question_type_note: A structure question is answered by what each paragraph does, not by what it is about. Name the moves in your own words first, then look for the option with the same number of moves in the same order.
explanation.reading_habit: Before reading structural options, write a verb for each paragraph. An option that offers three verbs for a four-move passage has left a paragraph unaccounted for, and that is usually the paragraph carrying the argument.

distractors.why_wrong: Nothing in the passage is corrected as a mistake of fact, and the courts' test is refused rather than defended: the classifying question is said to ask in the form of a label something that is plainly a matter of degree.
distractors.seductive_element: The opening really does show a description failing, and readers expect a passage that unseats a popular view to end by endorsing the official one.

distractors.why_wrong: Only one account is attributed to anybody else. The classical definition is not offered as a rival theory to be weighed against the market description but as the thing that dissolves the puzzle, and no view is discarded as the weaker of two.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the live rival, because the passage does contain two ways of describing a platform and does end by extending an old definition to a new case, so three of its elements are present and only the adjudication is invented.

distractors.why_wrong: No losses are counted anywhere and no prediction is made about the speed of legal reform. The last paragraph is about what a better test would need, not about how long the law will take to adopt one.
distractors.seductive_element: Writing about platform work usually does itemise harms and complain of a lagging law, and readers supply the genre's standard furniture.

questions.target_mistake: taking the description the passage opens by refusing, that platform work is the market reclaiming ground from the firm, as the passage's own position
questions.prediction_target: The learner should be able to say before the options: a platform directs without employing, so two lines that used to coincide have separated, and obligations belong on the first of them.
questions.stem: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Platform work has returned labour to the market, so the protections designed for the payroll era are attached to a form of employment now in decline.
options.B: The classical definition of the firm is refuted by the platforms, and a definition built instead on who bears the risk of an idle hour should replace it.
options.C: Platforms direct work without employing anyone, so the firm's boundary and the employment relation's boundary have separated, and obligations should follow direction rather than contractual form.
options.D: Courts asked to place platform workers in one of two categories have reached conflicting results, and a test of degree would give the law the consistency it now lacks.

explanation.expert_notice: The third paragraph carries the thesis and states it as a separation: two boundaries that lay on top of each other, one marking where direction replaces bargaining and one marking where obligations attach, are pulled apart by a platform. The fourth paragraph then puts the obligations back on the first of the two.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option holds the diagnosis and the remedy together, which is what the passage's own shape requires. The second paragraph earns the first half by showing that a platform meets the classical test for a firm in every respect but employment; the third states the separation; the fourth argues that a duty framed for a matter of degree should be measured in degrees rather than decided by a label. An option that stops before the remedy leaves the last paragraph unexplained, and one that omits the separation leaves the third.
explanation.question_type_note: In a passage that diagnoses and then prescribes, the main idea contains both. Test a candidate by asking which paragraph it would allow you to delete.
explanation.reading_habit: When a passage says that two things which used to coincide have come apart, write both of them down separately. Every later claim in such a passage is about which of the two something should be attached to.

distractors.why_wrong: This is the description the opening paragraph attributes to the arrangement's friends and critics alike, and the passage refuses it in the next breath by showing that platforms set prices, allocate buyers and penalise refusal. On the author's account direction has not gone to the market at all; only the contract has.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the received wisdom about platform work, it is stated in the passage's own opening sentences, and nothing labels it as somebody else's view until the awkwardness is named.

distractors.why_wrong: The classical definition is the instrument of the argument, not its target. The passage uses it to show that a platform is a firm, and the risk of an idle hour is lifted out of the list of obligations that attach to employment and re-used here as a definition of the firm, which is a job the passage never gives it.
distractors.seductive_element: A passage that says a familiar description fails invites the expectation that some definition is about to be overturned, and the idle hour is a vivid phrase lying close to hand.

distractors.why_wrong: Conflicting decisions are never mentioned and consistency is never the complaint. The objection to classification is that it answers in the form of a label a condition the passage calls plainly a matter of degree, and the closing sentences say the graded test would leave the problem of proof exactly where it was.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the live rival, because it names the passage's own remedy and supplies the motive a reader expects a legal argument to have, which makes the substituted reason hard to see.

questions.target_mistake: taking the reason people submit to direction, which the passage gives in the same sentence, for the definition of a firm
questions.stem: According to the passage, the classical account defines a firm by

options.A: the existence of a payroll, together with the continuing obligations owed to those on it
options.B: the replacement of bargaining by instruction, whatever the legal form of the relation
options.C: the power to set a price that a competitive market would not have produced
options.D: a scale of operation at which bargaining over each transaction becomes too costly, whatever is being sold

explanation.expert_notice: The second paragraph does the work in two consecutive sentences. It first rules out payroll, premises and longevity, and then supplies the definition in the form of a substitution: instruction is put in the place of price, so that what gets done is settled by one person telling another.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option is that definition with its consequence attached. Because the test is about how decisions are made and not about the paperwork that records the relation, a platform can satisfy it while employing nobody, which is precisely the use the passage goes on to make of it. Reading the definition correctly is what makes the rest of the argument available.
explanation.question_type_note: A detail question about a definition is decided by the sentence that defines, not by the sentence that explains why the thing defined exists. They often sit side by side.
explanation.reading_habit: When a passage says what something is not before saying what it is, mark the rejected list. Distractors in detail questions are built out of it far more often than out of anything else.

distractors.why_wrong: The paragraph names the payroll first among the things the classical account does not define a firm by, and the whole argument depends on that exclusion, since a platform is then shown to be a firm although it employs nobody.
distractors.seductive_element: A payroll is what most readers think a firm is, and the obligations owed to those on it are listed in the passage a paragraph later, which makes the phrase feel supported.

distractors.why_wrong: The passage never discusses market power or what price a competitive market would have produced. Price-setting appears only as one of three signs that a platform is not behaving as a market, and a sign is not a definition.
distractors.seductive_element: The opening does say that the platform sets the price where a market would let a seller post it, and price-setting is the mark of a firm most readers already carry with them.

distractors.why_wrong: The cost of bargaining is given as the reason anybody submits to instruction, not as what makes an organisation a firm. Scale is nowhere in the passage, and a small operation that settles its work by instruction would satisfy the definition as written.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the live rival, because the cost of separate bargains appears in the very sentence that carries the definition, and readers take the clause that explains for the clause that defines.

questions.target_mistake: concluding that a classifying court must now decide cases wrongly, when the passage says only that it is testing at the wrong line
questions.prediction_target: The learner should predict that the answer will locate the court's question on one of the two boundaries the third paragraph separates.
questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that a court deciding platform cases by asking whether the worker is an employee or an independent contractor

options.A: will usually decide for the worker, since direction through an interface is conspicuous and easy to establish
options.B: is applying a test that worked because employment was, in that era, the commoner way of organising work
options.C: is looking for the obligations at the line the contract marks and not at the line where direction begins
options.D: will reach a different answer from a court that asked how far the worker had been directed

explanation.expert_notice: The third paragraph sets out two lines and says why they used to be one. Obligations attach at the employment line; direction operates at the firm's line; the law took the contract as its evidence of direction because the two coincided. A classifying question asks about the contract, which is to ask at the line that no longer carries what is being looked for.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option states that mismatch and nothing more. The court's question is about the form of the relation, and the passage has just shown that on a platform the form of the relation and the exercise of direction have separated, so the answer to the court's question no longer tells it what it is asking the question in order to find out. The inference is one step from the sentence about obligations being fixed to the contract rather than to the direction.
explanation.question_type_note: An inference question about a procedure asks what the procedure is actually testing for. Locate the test on the passage's own map before looking at the options.
explanation.reading_habit: When an author says a rule once used one thing as evidence of another, ask what happens to the rule when the two come apart. That question is the inference such passages are built to support.

distractors.why_wrong: The passage never says which way classification cases come out, or that direction is easy to prove. Its closing sentences say the opposite about proof, since the record of how much direction a platform exercises is held by the platform.
distractors.seductive_element: The second paragraph lists five kinds of direction in one sentence, which makes direction look conspicuous and therefore easy to demonstrate in a court.

distractors.why_wrong: The reason given for the old test's soundness is not that employment was common but that direction was administered through a contract of service, so the contract was evidence of the direction. A rare arrangement with the same structure would have been tested just as well.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the live rival, because the passage does say the test once worked and no longer does, and prevalence is the readiest explanation of why a legal category fits an era.

distractors.why_wrong: The passage claims a separation, not a reversal. A worker who is heavily directed and also carries the label of employee would be treated the same way by both tests, and the argument for grading is about the many intermediate cases rather than about universal disagreement.
distractors.seductive_element: Two tests that look at different things feel as though they must disagree, and the passage's insistence that the lines have come apart encourages the stronger reading.

vocabulary.meaning_here: the putting of one thing in the place of another

vocabulary.passage_use: A market lets a buyer choose among sellers; the platform allocates
vocabulary.meaning_here: assigns work to a particular person rather than letting the choice be made

mentor.challenge: A familiar claim about platform work is set against what platforms actually do, and the passage then says that the change everybody has noticed is not the change that happened. Keep hold of the two boundaries the third paragraph separates, because three of the four questions are decided there.
mentor.one_sentence_summary: Platform work is usually described as the market taking ground back from the firm, but platforms fix prices, allocate customers and penalise refusal, and on the classical definition, which turns on the substitution of instruction for price rather than on payroll, a platform is a firm that directs without employing, so the boundary of the firm and the boundary of the employment relation, which coincided for a century because direction ran through a contract of service, have come apart, which argues for attaching obligations in proportion to the direction exercised rather than to a label, at the cost of needing a measure that only the platform holds.
mentor.main_idea: The classical account defines a firm by the replacement of bargaining with instruction, and by that test a platform is a thorough firm that happens to employ nobody. Because obligations were attached to the contract of service, and the contract used to be where direction lived, the protections now sit at a line the direction has left. The remedy is to grade obligations by how much direction is exercised, and its difficulty is that the evidence for such a grading is in the platform's own records.
mentor.simple_explanation:
When app companies started handing out short driving jobs, everybody described it the same way, whether they liked it or not: the market is coming back, work is being bought job by job again, and the big organisation is breaking up into lots of little contracts.

The author says there is something wrong with that description. Platforms do not act like markets at all. In a market, a seller says what he charges; here the platform decides. In a market, a customer picks his seller; here the platform assigns one. In a market, turning down a bad offer is just information about what a seller thinks he is worth; here turning down work is logged as a fault against you.

So what is a firm, exactly? The old economic definition does not say it is a thing with a payroll, a building and a long life. It says a firm is the place where instructions replace prices. Inside a firm, work happens because somebody tells somebody else to do it, and people put up with being told because haggling over every single job separately would cost more than being told costs. Judged that way, a platform is a firm, and a very controlling one. It sets the price, the route, the order of the jobs, the standard of the work and the terms on which you are dropped. The only thing it does not do is employ you.

Now the important part. For about a hundred years there were two different lines that sat exactly on top of each other, so nobody needed to tell them apart. Line one is where a firm begins: where being told replaces bargaining. Line two is where employment begins: where a set of legal duties turns up, like notice, a minimum rate, responsibility if you get hurt, and who pays for an hour with no work in it. They sat together because being told what to do came through an employment contract, so the law used the contract as proof that somebody was being directed.

A platform separates the two lines. The directing happens through an app. The contract says you are running your own little business. And the legal duties, because they were pinned to the contract rather than to the directing, go wherever the contract goes.

So what should be done? Courts are being asked the wrong question. They are asked to put a person in one of two boxes: employee or contractor. But the thing those duties were invented for, one side setting all the terms while the other carries the consequences, is obviously a matter of more and less. It should be answered in more and less. A test that measured how much direction there was, and gave protection in proportion, would match reality better than any two-box test can.

And then the honest ending. Such a test needs a measurement, and the only running record of how much a platform directs anybody is the record the platform itself keeps. So grading the test does not make the problem of proof go away. It just moves it: instead of arguing about what to call a worker, you argue about what a company can be forced to hand over.
mentor.why_difficult: The opening states the popular description without marking it as somebody else's, so a reader who fixes the thesis early carries away the view the passage exists to refuse. The second difficulty is the definition, which arrives in the same sentence as the reason people accept direction, and the two are easy to swap. The third is the third paragraph, which is the argument: it asks the reader to hold two boundaries apart that the whole of ordinary language treats as one, and every later claim depends on which of the two a thing is attached to. The last paragraph then refuses to let its own remedy be comfortable, which readers expecting a solution tend to skim.
mentor.author_intention: To move the reader off the question everybody argues about, whether platform work is employment, and onto the question the author thinks is underneath it, which is how much direction is being exercised and where the evidence of it is kept.

paragraph_journey.note: Everyone says platforms are the market coming back. But platforms set prices, hand out customers and punish refusal, which is not what markets do.
A firm is not a payroll. A firm is where instructions replace prices. By that test a platform is a firm, and a strict one, that employs nobody.
Two lines used to sit on top of each other: where direction starts, and where legal duties start. The platform pulls them apart, and the duties follow the contract.
Stop asking which label fits. Measure how much direction there is and protect in proportion. The catch is that the measurement lives in the platform's own records.

mentor.tone_progression: It opens level and slightly amused at a description everybody shares, becomes precise and definitional in the middle where the argument is made, and closes practical and unsentimental, proposing a remedy and immediately declining to pretend that it settles anything.
key_transitions: 'The description has one awkwardness.' (paragraph 1): the received account is put against the conduct it is supposed to describe.
'That is the change, and it is not the change usually reported.' (opening of paragraph 3): the thesis arrives as a correction of what people think they have noticed.
'Grading the test does not dispose of the problem of proof.' (paragraph 4): the remedy is granted and its limit stated in the same breath.
mentor.misunderstanding: The commonest wrong model is that the passage is an attack on platform companies for avoiding employment law, which would make the remedy a demand that they employ people. It is not: the author's point is that employment was only ever the law's evidence of something else, and his remedy attaches duties to that something else rather than to the status. The opposite wrong model reads the last paragraph as a solution and comes away believing the author has fixed the problem, when the final two sentences say the difficulty has been relocated rather than removed.
mentor.traps_summary: This set offers the received description as the thesis, the reason people accept direction as the definition of a firm, an invented complaint about inconsistent courts, and a reversal where the passage claims only a separation. Sorting each option into description, definition, diagnosis or remedy answers all four.
mentor.reading_lesson: When an author says that two things which used to coincide have come apart, stop and write them in two columns, because every subsequent claim in such a passage is a claim about which column something belongs in, and the distractors will be built by putting it in the other one. The companion habit is to read the last sentence of a prescriptive passage with particular care: an author who names the cost of his own remedy has ruled out every option that presents the remedy as a settlement.
mentor.real_world: The same separation is worth looking for wherever a legal category was built as a proxy for something harder to observe: residence standing in for connection to a place, a job title standing in for responsibility, a registered address standing in for where a business really operates. In each, the interesting question is what the proxy was evidence of, and whether the thing it was evidence of is still at the same address.
mentor.takeaway: A firm is not a payroll; it is wherever somebody is told rather than asked.
mentor.reflection_question: In the arrangements you are part of, how much of what you do is settled by a price you agreed and how much by an instruction you received?
